required_denominator: annual Boeing family/cohort departures for 2010-2025 under a compatible global commercial-jet scope

sources.source_title: Annual Safety Report Annex 4 sector tables + World Air Transport Statistics aircraft-use releases
sources.observed_granularity: global annual sectors/flights by manufacturer/model for overlapping historical windows; recent WATS aircraft-model frequency observations
sources.reason: Public Annex 4 editions demonstrate model-level global sector counts across at least 2010-2019, and WATS exposes recent 2024-2025 Boeing 737 all-variant frequencies. However a continuous 2020-2023 public bridge is not yet demonstrated and Boeing 737 is aggregated across variants, so NG/737-800 and MAX 8 exposure cannot be separated without an additional authoritative mapping/source. Historical values are also revision-sensitive and require a declared vintage rule.

sources.source_title: 2025 Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents
sources.observed_granularity: annual worldwide all-commercial-jet departures/flight-hours plus cumulative Boeing/type statistics
sources.reason: No complete annual Boeing-family departures/cycles matrix for the preregistered 2010-2025 cohort-year cells has been demonstrated. Aggregate or cumulative values cannot be disaggregated or inverted.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation / Bureau of Transportation Statistics
sources.observed_granularity: monthly non-stop segment records by aircraft type/service class with scheduled/performed departures and aircraft hours
sources.reason: The database covers U.S. domestic operations and international operations with at least one U.S./territory service point; foreign-to-foreign flights are excluded. It can support sensitivity/reconciliation work but cannot serve as the global BSFM family-year denominator.

sources.source_title: ICAO Long Term Traffic Forecast application
sources.observed_granularity: historical traffic by carrier/country-pair/route-group/region plus forecasts of departures and fleet forecasts by aircraft type
sources.reason: The public product description does not establish a reproducible historical actual-departures matrix at Boeing-family-by-year granularity matching the BSFM denominator. Forecasted departures/fleet are not substitutes for historical measured exposure, and no new paid ICAO API dependency is permitted.

prohibited_transformations: allocate aggregate departures to Boeing families using fleet share
split Boeing 737 all-variant sectors into NG/737-800/MAX using fleet share, deliveries or accident counts
invert cumulative accident rates to reconstruct annual family departures
use fleet counts, deliveries, capacity or market share as the primary denominator
substitute forecast departures for historical measured departures

conclusion.next_research_direction: Prioritize a sustainable 2020-2023 bridge and variant-level 737 exposure source or a preregistered cohort design demonstrably compatible with the available global model-sector data; otherwise retain the denominator gap.
